boxed-text.p: Yu H, Liu D, Zhang Y, Tang R, Fan X, Mao S, Lv L, Chen F, Qin H, Zhang Z, van Aalten DMF, Yang B, Yuan K. 2024. Tissue-specific O-GlcNAcylation profiling identifies substrates in translational machinery in Drosophila mushroom body contributing to olfactory learning. eLife 13:e91269. doi: 10.7554/eLife.91269.

body.p: During an internal review, we identified errors in Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and their source data. We checked the affected source-data files and figures against the original experimental records and repeated the relevant analyses where necessary. We corrected the affected source data and regenerated the affected panels using the verified original data and corrected analyses. None of these corrections affects the main conclusions of the study. We sincerely apologize for these errors.

The discrepancies arose at several manual steps during preparation of the source-data files and composite figures. During the study, separate working datasets were generated for different analytical strategies and for parallel experiments using the same experimental groups. Source-data tables were subsequently compiled manually from these working files, and the final multi-panel figures were assembled from editable graphical elements in Adobe Illustrator. As detailed below, these steps led to distinct panel-specific errors that were not identified during our pre-publication checks.

Figure 4A: We initially defined the Brain Neuron population by averaging values from the mushroom body, antennal lobe, ellipsoid body and optic lobe. We later refined this strategy by incorporating additional neuronal cell types, providing a more comprehensive representation of the Brain Neuron population. The updated strategy was used for all subsequent analyses and for preparation of Supplementary files 10 and 11. The two strategies yielded identical values for the other cell populations and differed only in the calculated Brain Neuron values. However, during preparation of the Figure 4A source data and heatmap, we inadvertently used the Brain Neuron mRNA-level values generated using the initial strategy rather than the updated strategy. In addition, RpS30 mRNA values, which are not shown in Figure 4A, were entered in place of the corresponding RpS3 values. Separately, when generating the lower heatmap of normalized O-GlcNAc levels, the positions of RpS5a and RpS6 were inadvertently reversed relative to the upper mRNA-level heatmap, causing the normalized O-GlcNAc values for these two genes to be displayed under the incorrect gene labels. We corrected the affected entries in the source data and regenerated Figure 4A using the corrected data.

Figure 4C: A visiting student conducted a parallel set of experiments using the same experimental groups under our supervision. These experiments were performed separately from the primary experiments used for Figure 4C. During preparation of the Figure 4C source-data file, measurements from the visiting student’s parallel experiments were inadvertently entered into the corresponding data table. Because the two datasets used the same group designations, the table labels remained unchanged although the numerical values differed. We checked the original experimental records and the GraphPad Prism file used to generate Figure 4C and confirmed that the published statistical analysis was based on the primary experimental dataset rather than the measurements entered in the uploaded source-data file. We therefore corrected the source-data file using the measurements from the primary experiment. Separately, comparison of the GraphPad Prism graph with the published Figure 4C showed that the graph had been inadvertently stretched vertically during assembly in Adobe Illustrator. We regenerated Figure 4C using the verified primary dataset and restored the graph’s original proportions.

Figure 4E: During compilation of the source-data file, one set of OPP fluorescence-intensity measurements (17.54 for mushroom body, 23.71 for whole brain, and 0.74 for the relative intensity ratio) was inadvertently omitted from the OK107-Gal4>CpOGAWT group, and one P value was incorrectly entered as 0.01 instead of 0.001. In addition, during assembly of the multi-panel figure in Adobe Illustrator, the highest data point in the OK107-Gal4>CpOGADM group was inadvertently omitted, and one data point in the OK107-Gal4>CpOGAWT group was displaced when the panel was repositioned. The statistical-significance asterisks for both comparisons were also incorrectly annotated in the figure. We restored the omitted measurements, corrected the statistical information, and regenerated Figure 4E directly from the complete original dataset. The corrected P values for the two comparisons are 0.00057 and 0.00097, respectively. The direction and interpretation of the result are unchanged.
We have corrected the source data for Figure 4 panels A, C and E (Figure 4—source data 3).

Figure 4—figure supplement 1B: During source-data compilation, normalized O-GlcNAc values from Table S11 were mistakenly entered into the “O-GlcNAc levels” column, and several mRNA values (C43:C47) were assigned to the wrong rows after the gene order in the source-data table was rearranged. In addition, the incorrect RpS3 mRNA value entered during preparation of Figure 4A was carried into the corresponding analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B. We corrected the affected source-data entries and regenerated panel B using the corrected data. The associated P value and R² were recalculated and updated to 0.1919 and 0.0402, respectively.

Figure 4—figure supplement 1D: The P values entered in the published source-data file were calculated from comparisons with the OK107-Gal4 control rather than with the corresponding OK107-Gal4>Luciferase RNAi control. In addition, during assembly of the multi-panel figure in Adobe Illustrator, errors were inadvertently introduced when adjusting the plotted data points, resulting in two extra points being displayed in the OK107-Gal4>RPS26 RNAi group and one point being omitted from the OK107-Gal4>RPS3 RNAi group. We corrected the P values in the source data and regenerated panel D using the corrected data. In the corrected panel, the comparison between OK107-Gal4>RPL5 RNAi and OK107-Gal4>Luciferase RNAi is statistically significant (P=0.036), whereas it was previously shown as non-significant. The remaining comparisons and the overall interpretation are unchanged.
We have corrected the source data for Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and 1D (Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
The corrected Figure 4—figure supplement 1 (updated panels B and D) is shown here:

No changes to the main text or figure legends are required.
The article has been corrected accordingly.
